name: 深度分析问题编译器
purpose: Separate description, explanation, prediction, intervention-effect estimation, and action selection; compile the decision question and observed data shape into independent analytical layers, claim boundaries, missing identification evidence, and executable probe recommendations.
eligibility_checks: the source scope and analysis unit are known
the task requires more than a simple lookup, formula, or summary
at least one observable outcome is named
assumptions: analysis depth is determined by the strongest supported claim, not method complexity or report length
description, prediction, causal explanation, and decision optimization are different objectives
time-dependent prediction must be evaluated without future leakage and with paired uncertainty for model differences
data-driven subgroup discovery must use non-overlapping units for confirmation
logged-policy evaluation must expose propensity overlap and sensitivity to weight handling
design evidence must identify the same unit, outcome, intervention, comparator, group mapping, and estimand as the compiled question
human_gates: review the causal graph, identifying assumptions, intervention definition, planned estimator, and decision utility when those layers are requested
confirm that executed identification-check evidence is separate from the experiment plan and semantically bound to the exact check
outputs: independent readiness for measurement, descriptive, temporal, heterogeneity, mechanism, causal, predictive, and decision layers
claim-family permissions without an overall depth score
frozen honest or prespecified heterogeneity, direct-mechanism, uncertainty-aware predictive competition, causal, and scenario or logged-policy targets
the source question specification needed for fresh recompilation before advanced finding adoption
diagnostics: observational causal question lacks an identification strategy or confounder review
time-dependent prediction uses random splitting, in-sample accuracy, or lacks paired-loss uncertainty
data-driven subgroup discovery reuses estimation units
decision recommendation lacks alternatives, value, costs, constraints, overlap diagnostics, sensitivity, or a threshold
evidence_requirements: verified evidence for the outcome and declared data readiness
explicit intervention, comparator, time zero, follow-up, and estimand for causal questions
a future-safe holdout design for predictive questions
decision alternatives and downside for action selection
allowed_claims: a named analytical layer is ready, conditional, blocked, or not requested
the current evidence supports only descriptive, associational, mechanism-hypothesis, predictive, causal, or decision claims as separately stated
a particular missing observation or assumption prevents a stronger claim
forbidden_claims: an overall depth score hides a blocked analytical layer
a complex estimator upgrades association to causation
a causal estimate is ready without a well-defined intervention and identification strategy
a decision follows from an estimate without value, cost, constraints, and a threshold
